claim: An optogenetic approach using caged cyclofen (cCYC) can control the activity of proteins fused to the ERT-receptor in vivo.
source: Optogenetics approaches allow for the photocontrol and monitoring of the activity of biomolecules in vivo. The approach we developed uses a photoactivable analog of tamoxifen (caged cyclofen [cCYC]) to control the activity of proteins fused to the ERT-receptor (Sinha et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2018) (a modified estrogen binding domain; Feil et al., 1996; Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and use of an optogenetic system with caged cyclofen, supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Proteins fused to ERT-receptor are sequestered by cytoplasmic chaperones until cCYC is uncaged by light.
source: These protein constructs are sequestered by cytoplasmic chaperones. Once cCYC is uncaged by light (with one-photon illumination at ~375 nm or two-photon at ~750 nm), cyclofen (CYC) is released (Sinha et al., 2010).
evidence: The mechanism is described in the text and supported by citation to Sinha et al., 2010.

claim: Cyclofen binds to the ERT-receptor and releases the fused protein from its complex with cytoplasmic chaperones.
source: It binds to the ERT-receptor and releases the fused protein (e.g. a Cre-ERT recombinase) from its complex with cytoplasmic chaperones (Zhang et al., 2018; Figure 1A).
evidence: The mechanism is described in text with citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: A transgenic zebrafish line was engineered to express KRASG12V oncogene upon photoactivation of CRE-ERT.
source: We used this approach to photocontrol the activity of a Cre/loxP recombination system in a transgenic zebrafish line (Tgactin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP; ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP) carrying a floxable (loxP flanked) EOS gene (coding for a green fluorescent protein) upstream from the oncogene (Feng et al., 2017; Sinha et al., 2010) (KRASG12V).
evidence: The transgenic line construction is described with citations to prior work.

claim: Whole body expression of KRASG12V oncogene at 1 day post-fertilization did not result in tumorigenesis.
source: Consistent with an acquired refractory cell state and a loss of oncogenic competence (Baggiolini et al., 2021), whole body expression of the oncogene at 1 day post-fertilization (dpf) did not result in tumorigenesis.
evidence: The observation is stated with citation to support the interpretation.

claim: In absence of illumination, no spontaneous uncaging of cCYC and activation of the oncogene is observed.
source: Notice that consistent with previous studies (Feng et al., 2017; Sinha et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2018), where cCYC stability has been validated both in vitro (by chemical analyses) and in vivo (with fluorescent reporters of uncaging), in absence of illumination no spontaneous uncaging of cCYC and thus activation of the oncogene (i.e. blue fluorescent cells) is observed.
evidence: The observation is supported by citations to previous validation studies.

claim: Activation of KRASG12V at 1 dpf followed by transient activation of Ventx, Nanog, or Oct4 yields reproducible hyperplasic outgrowths in multiple tissues.
source: Activation of the oncogene (Feng et al., 2017) at 1 dpf, if and only if followed by transient activation of Ventx (or Nanog or Oct4), did yield reproducible hyperplasic outgrowths in many different tissues (including brain, intestine, pancreas, and liver; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The experimental result is described with reference to supplementary figures showing the data.

claim: Hyperplasic tissues induced by KRASG12V plus Ventx display phospho-ERK activity.
source: Immunohistochemistry detection of phospho-ERK activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B), hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C), decreased survival (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D), and reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) of selected genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Figure 1—figure supplement 6A and B) all display features associated with tumorigenesis.
evidence: Multiple experimental assays are described with references to figures showing the data.

claim: None of the controls (activation of kRasG12V only, Ventx-GR only, incubation in CYC or DEX) developed hyperplasia.
source: None of the controls (activation of kRasG12V only, Ventx-GR only, incubation in CYC or DEX, etc.) developed hyperplasia, but rather grew into normal zebrafish (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Control experiments are described with references to figures.

claim: The observed tumor is only a result of the joint activation of kRasG12V (permanently) and a reprogramming factor (transiently).
source: These controls imply that the observed tumor is only a result of the joint activation of kRasG12V (permanently) and a reprogramming factor (transiently).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the control experiments described.

claim: Both kRasG12V and Ventx have been reported to play a role in brain cancer.
source: Since both kRasG12V and Ventx have been reported to play a role in brain cancer (Lam et al., 2022), we decided to activate the oncogene kRasG12V at 1 dpf in a single normal cell of the brain of a transgenic zebrafish (injected with the mRNA of Ventx-GR at one-cell stage).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lam et al., 2022.

claim: Activation of the oncogene in a single cell was achieved by 1 hr incubation in cCYC, followed by washing and illumination at 405 nm in a small area of the brain.
source: Activation of the oncogene in a single cell was achieved by 1 hr incubation in cCYC, followed by washing and illumination at 405 nm to uncage cCYC in a small area (diameter ~80 μm) of the brain (in the vicinity of the otic vesicle) (Figure 1G).
evidence: The experimental procedure is described with reference to Figure 1G.

claim: With probability ~50%, the oncogene is activated in a single cell of the illuminated area following cCYC uncaging.
source: Subsequent to cCYC uncaging, with probability ~50% the oncogene is activated in a single cell of the illuminated area (activation statistics is shown in Figure 2A), identified within ~1 hr by the blue fluorescence of its nuclear marker (H2B-mTFP), see Figures 1G and 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
evidence: The probability is stated with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: H2B-mTFP positive cells are only observed at the site of illumination, attesting to the precision of the optogenetic method.
source: H2B-mTFP positive cells are only observed at the site of illumination (i.e. brain), attesting to the precision of our optogenetic method (Figure 2A).
evidence: The observation is described with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Activation of the oncogene alone does not give rise to cancer; the activated cell usually disappears within a few days.
source: Notice that activation of the oncogene alone does not give rise to cancer (the activated cell usually disappears within a few days, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), which implies that the proliferation of kRasG12V positive (mTFP+, blue fluorescent) cells - reported next - is not due to late activation of the oncogene (and its fluorescent marker).
evidence: The observation is described with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: If and only if following the local expression of the oncogene, Ventx-GR is transiently activated does the cell divide and proliferate.
source: Indeed, if and only if following the local expression of the oncogene, Ventx-GR is transiently activated (by 24 hr incubation in DEX) does the cell divide and proliferate (Figure 2B and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The experimental result is described with references to multiple figures.

claim: At 1 day post-induction, ~50% of the induced cells had divided and expanded clonally by a factor ~3.
source: We observed that at 1 day post-induction (dpi) ~50% of the induced cells had divided and expanded clonally by a factor ~3 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The quantitative observation is described with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: In the other 50% of cases at 1 dpi, the activated single cell had neither divided nor died.
source: In the other 50% of cases, the activated single cell had neither divided nor died (Figure 2B).
evidence: The observation is described with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: At 3-5 dpi, in all zebrafish larvae (n=30) the induced cell(s) gave rise to progeny that display short-range dispersion and then give rise to a tumor mass in the brain.
source: Surprisingly, at 3–5 dpi, we observed in all zebrafish larvae (n=30) that the induced cell(s) gave rise to progeny that display short-range dispersion (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B) and then give rise to a tumor mass in the brain with local infiltration of malignant cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: The observation is described with sample size and references to figures.

claim: H&E staining of the brain tissue and metastases confirm the malignant state of the induced cell and its progeny.
source: H&E staining of the brain tissue (Figure 2D and E) and metastases (Figure 3) further confirm the malignant state of the induced cell and its progeny.
evidence: Histological analysis is described with references to figures.

claim: Some cells of the progeny re-localized to new loci far from the brain, such as the heart, digestive tract, and trunk.
source: In parallel with tumor mass formation in the brain (Figure 2), we observed that some cells of the progeny re-localized to new loci far from the brain, such as the heart (Figure 3A), the digestive tract (Figure 3B; Figure 2—figure supplement 4D), and the trunk (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B; Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: The observation is described with references to multiple figures.

claim: The transient activation of Ventx alters the state of a cell expressing KRASG12V and induces its malignant transformation in vivo, with tumorigenic potential and capacity to generate invasive progeny.
source: We therefore deduce that the transient activation of Ventx alters the state of a cell expressing a mutated oncogene (i.e. KRASG12V) and induces its malignant transformation in vivo, with tumorigenic potential and the capacity to generate invasive progeny.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Metastatic cells must be the progeny of the initial blue fluorescent cell as the larvae are incubated in embryo medium with no cCYC.
source: Notice that metastatic cells must be the progeny of the initial (blue fluorescent) cell as the larvae are incubated in embryo medium with no cCYC.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental conditions.

claim: Absent VentX activation, proliferation and metastatic behavior are not observed; rather the initially induced cell disappears.
source: Furthermore, absent VentX activation we do not observe proliferation and metastatic behavior, rather the initially induced cell disappears, see Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.
evidence: The control observation is described with reference to a figure.

claim: Of the larvae in which a few (1-6) cells were expressing the oncogene and in which Ventx was transiently activated, all (N=30) developed tumors within 5 dpi.
source: Of the larvae in which a few (1–6) cells were expressing the oncogene and in which Ventx was transiently activated (KR+VX cell), all (N=30) developed tumors within 5 dpi.
evidence: The quantitative result is stated with sample size.

claim: The frequency of tumor development from KR+VX cells is F1=1.
source: The frequency of tumor development is therefore F1=1.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental data.

claim: The probability for a KR+VX cell to not develop a tumor is F0=0.
source: Conversely, the probability for such a cell to not develop a tumor is F0=0.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental data.

claim: The probability of tumor development from a single KR+VX cell is estimated to be P1>80% (χ2=3.75; df = 1).
source: Due to the finite size of the sample, we estimate the probability of tumor development from a single cell to be: P1>80% (χ2=3.75; df = 1).
evidence: This is a statistical estimate based on the experimental data.

claim: A single cell isolated from hyperplasic tissue and injected into a naïve host zebrafish larva led to integration, migration, and colonization of the host tissues by the progeny of the transplanted cell.
source: To definitely confirm the carcinogenic nature of the KR+VX-induced cells, we isolated and injected a single cell from a hyperplasic tissue (identified by the blue fluorescence of its nucleus) into a naïve host zebrafish larva. This led to integration, migration, and colonization of the host tissues by the progeny of the transplanted cell (Figure 4A and B), with strong pERK activity detected in tumor masses of the host (Figure 4B).
evidence: The transplantation experiment is described with references to figures.

claim: Out of 52 transplanted host zebrafish, 31 developed tumors, a probability of 60%.
source: Out of 52 transplanted host zebrafish, 31 developed tumors, a probability of tumor development (60%) consistent with previously reported efficiency of tumor cells transplantation in zebrafish (Campbell et al., 2021).
evidence: The quantitative result is stated with citation to prior work for comparison.

claim: The capacity of the progeny of the induced cells to metastasize and develop a tumor mass when transplanted in a naïve zebrafish is the operational definition of a malignant tumor.
source: The capacity of the progeny of the induced cells to metastasize and develop a tumor mass when transplanted in a naïve zebrafish is - to the best of our knowledge - the operational definition of a malignant tumor.
evidence: This is a statement about the definition used in the field.

claim: Injection into a naïve larva of an oncogene expressing cell which did not experience the transient activation of a reprogramming factor does not yield a tumor and disappears within a few days.
source: Notice that injection into a naïve larva of an oncogene expressing cell (identified by its nuclear blue fluorescence) which did not experience the transient activation of a reprogramming factor does not yield a tumor and disappears within a few days (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The control experiment is described with reference to a figure.

claim: Many cells may harbor oncogenic mutations, but only a few unpredictably end up developing a full-blown tumor.
source: While many cells may harbor oncogenic mutations, only a few unpredictably end up developing a full-blown tumor (Cairns, 1975; Riva et al., 2020; Adashek et al., 2020; Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the field supported by multiple citations.

claim: Various theories have been proposed to explain the transition from normal cell to tumor, but none has been tested in vivo at the single-cell level.
source: Various theories have been proposed to explain that transition (Soto and Sonnenschein, 2011; Tomasetti and Vogelstein, 2015; Jassim et al., 2023; Waclaw et al., 2015), but none has been tested in vivo at the single-cell level.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field supported by citations.

claim: Cancer initiation is believed to be a rare event taking place at the level of individual cells.
source: Cancer initiation is thus believed to be a rare event taking place at the level of individual cells (Visvader, 2011; Nowell, 1976; Hanahan, 2022; Pénisson et al., 2022; Frumkin et al., 2008) arising as a result of the accumulation of genetic mutations in so-called Mut-driver genes (oncogenes such as KRAS [Malumbres and Barbacid, 2003; Pylayeva-Gupta et al., 2011], tumor suppressor genes [Strachan and Read, 1999] such as TP53 or lifespan [Blasco, 2005] genes such as TERT).
evidence: This is a statement about the field supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mutant KRAS is the most frequent driver of several cancers: about 27% of all human cancers, 45% of colorectal, and 90% of pancreatic cancers.
source: Notably, mutant KRAS is the most frequent driver of several cancers (COSMIC, 2024; Punekar et al., 2022): about 27% of all human cancers, 45% of colorectal, and 90% of pancreatic cancers (Merz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about cancer statistics supported by citations.

claim: Genes involved in embryonic development, pluri/multipotency, and cell reprogramming such as VENTX/NANOG and POU5/OCT4 are abnormally reactivated in late cancer stages.
source: Recently, it has been shown that genes involved in embryonic development, pluri/multipotency, and cell reprogramming such as VENTX/NANOG and POU5/OCT4 are abnormally reactivated in late cancer stages, where acting as Epigenetic Drivers (Epi-Drivers) they empower cancer cells with cancer stem cell (CSCs) features, resistance to anticancer therapies, and potential for cancer recurrence/relapse (Vogelstein et al., 2013; Hepburn et al., 2019; Villodre et al., 2016; Ducos et al., 2022; Rawat et al., 2010; Laise, 2022; Park et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings supported by multiple citations.

claim: Whether Epi-Drivers play a role during the early phases of malignant transformation is still unknown.
source: Although it is evident that such Epi-Drivers confer a selective advantage to CSCs in a full-blown cancer, whether they play a role during the early phases of malignant transformation is still unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in knowledge.

claim: Current approaches to the study of cancer use constitutive or conditional expression of Mut-driver or Epi-driver genes in specific tissues, even though only a small subset of these cells eventually leads to the growth of tumors.
source: Current approaches to the study of cancer use constitutive or conditional expression of Mut-driver (or Epi-driver genes; Shibata et al., 2018) in specific tissues, i.e., in many cells, even though only a small subset of these cells eventually leads to the growth of tumors (Adashek et al., 2020), often observed when the tumor already consists of many thousands of heterogeneous abnormal cells.
evidence: This is a statement about current methods supported by citations.

claim: Carcinogenetic processes observed among sibling organisms occur with variable latency period from the onset of induction, at different locations and develop asynchronously.
source: Hence, carcinogenetic processes observed among sibling organisms (Baggiolini et al., 2021; Ablain et al., 2018; Kaufman et al., 2016) occur with variable latency period from the onset of induction, at different locations and develop asynchronously.
evidence: This is a statement about observed phenomena supported by citations.

claim: The initial stages of tumorigenesis are difficult to study due to the rarity of the event in vivo.
source: As a result, the initial stages of tumorigenesis are difficult to study, the state of the cell(s) of origin difficult to assess and control while its cellular environment is perturbed by the induced expression of the Mut- or Epi-driver genes. Due to the rarity of the event in vivo (Kaufman et al., 2016), a statistically relevant single-cell tracking and characterization of the early stages of tumorigenesis has therefore never been done.
evidence: This is a statement about challenges in the field supported by citation.

claim: The synergy between KRASG12V and a reprogramming factor (Ventx, Nanog, or Oct4) increases the probability of carcinogenesis from a single cell by many orders of magnitude compared to the expression of either of these genes alone.
source: In the following we show the synergy between only two factors: the oncogene kRasG12V and a reprogramming factor (Ventx, Nanog, or Oct4) increases the probability of carcinogenesis from a single cell by many orders of magnitude when compared to the expression of either of these genes (or none).
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claim: The robust deterministic process of single-cell cancer induction suggests that the aberrant reactivation of Epi-Driver genes involved in reprogramming/pluripotency might be relevant to the irreversible malignant transformation of a cell.
source: The robust deterministic process of single-cell cancer induction that we uncovered suggests that the aberrant reactivation of Epi-Driver genes involved in reprogramming/pluripotency (such as VENTX/NANOG, POU5/OCT4) might be relevant to the irreversible malignant transformation of a cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Reprogramming Epi-Drivers are important regulators of cell viability, survival, and proliferation in several cellular contexts, from embryonic stem cells to cancer cells.
source: Reprogramming Epi-Drivers are important regulators of cell viability, survival, and proliferation in several cellular contexts, from embryonic stem cells to cancer cells (Hepburn et al., 2019; Villodre et al., 2016; Ducos et al., 2022; Rawat et al., 2010; Laise, 2022; Park et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the role of these factors supported by citations.

claim: Due to their capacity to modulate epigenetic memory and cell plasticity, reprogramming factors may drive the early stages of malignant transformation in vivo once reactivated aberrantly.
source: Due to their capacity to modulate epigenetic memory and cell plasticity, these reprogramming factors may drive the early stages of malignant transformation in vivo once (re)activated aberrantly.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings and known properties of these factors.

claim: Reprogramming factors likely share some mechanism(s) with processes such as induced nuclear reprogramming, pluripotency maintenance, and/or endogenous cell reprogramming during development.
source: They likely share some mechanism(s) with processes such as induced nuclear reprogramming (Hepburn et al., 2019; Villodre et al., 2016; Ducos et al., 2022), pluripotency maintenance, and/or endogenous cell reprogramming during development (Scerbo and Monsoro-Burq, 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to related work.

claim: The reactivation of the Neural Crest Progenitor program (possibly via the stochastic expression of VENTX/NANOG and/or POU5/OCT4) has been shown in BRAF/p53 double mutant cells to yield NC-related tumors in vivo.
source: Thus, consistent with our results, the reactivation (Scerbo and Monsoro-Burq, 2020) of the Neural Crest (NC) Progenitor program (possibly via the stochastic expression of VENTX/NANOG and/or POU5/OCT4) has been shown in BRAF/p53 double mutant cells to yield NC-related tumors in vivo (Baggiolini et al., 2021; Ablain et al., 2018; Kaufman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings supported by citations.

claim: Activation of Epi-Driver genes in NC-related tumors might confer predictable tumorigenesis.
source: We surmise that activation of Epi-Driver genes in NC-related tumors might confer predictable tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: Cells carrying cancer-causing mutations do not deterministically develop cancers in vivo.
source: Since cells carrying cancer-causing mutations do not deterministically developed cancers in vivo (Kaufman et al., 2016; Campbell et al., 2021), we suggest that the probability of a mutated cell to enter into malignant transformation, or to maintain its physiological functions despite mutations, correlates with the probability of the reactivation of reprogramming factors.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: The probability of a mutated cell to enter into malignant transformation correlates with the probability of the reactivation of reprogramming factors.
source: Since cells carrying cancer-causing mutations do not deterministically developed cancers in vivo (Kaufman et al., 2016; Campbell et al., 2021), we suggest that the probability of a mutated cell to enter into malignant transformation, or to maintain its physiological functions despite mutations, correlates with the probability of the reactivation of reprogramming factors.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings and prior work.

claim: The results support a 'Vogelgram' two-step model for irreversible single-cell malignant transformation in vivo, mirroring the two hits hypothesis proposed by Berenblum and Shubik, 1949.
source: Our results support a 'Vogelgram' (Fearon and Vogelstein, 1990) two-step model (Figure 5) for irreversible single-cell malignant transformation in vivo, mirroring the two hits hypothesis proposed by Berenblum and Shubik, 1949.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings with citations to prior models.

claim: The appearance of Mut-Drivers in a normal (preprocancer) cell within healthy tissue would act as a permissive but insufficient initiator for malignant cell transformation.
source: Thus, the appearance of Mut-Drivers in a normal (preprocancer; Brash, 2015) cell (Martincorena and Campbell, 2015) within healthy tissue would act as a permissive but insufficient initiator for malignant cell transformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings supported by citations.

claim: Surveillance mechanisms like cell competition between wild-type and mutated cells safeguard tissue homeostasis and result in active elimination of mutant cells from the tissue.
source: Despite the frequency of mutational insults, which are often caused by external cues (chemical carcinogens, UV, etc.) or senescence/aging, it is known that surveillance mechanisms like cell competition between wild-type and mutated cells safeguard tissue homeostasis and results in active elimination of mutant cells from the tissue (Brown et al., 2017; Porazinski et al., 2016; van Neerven and Vermeulen, 2023).
evidence: This is a statement about known mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: The aberrant reactivation of Epi-Driver genes involved in reprogramming/pluripotency may promote the irreversible and deterministic malignant transformation in the cell of origin of cancer leading to carcinogenesis.
source: Our data imply that the aberrant reactivation of Epi-Driver genes involved in reprogramming/pluripotency may promote the irreversible and deterministic malignant transformation in the cell of origin of cancer leading to carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The variation in cancer risk among tissues can be related to the number of stem cell divisions and tissue renewal.
source: Our hypothesis is further strengthened by the observation that the variation in cancer risk among tissues can be related to the number of stem cell divisions and tissue renewal (Tomasetti and Vogelstein, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings supported by citation.

claim: The aberrant reactivation (or maintenance) of Epi-Driver genes in regenerative events, in cooperation with incident mutations, might be the key deterministic factor in the switching of a normal/healthy cell into the first cell of origin of cancer.
source: The aberrant reactivation (or maintenance) of Epi-Driver genes in these regenerative events, in cooperation with incident mutations, might be the key deterministic factor in the switching of a normal/healthy cell into the first cell of origin of cancer.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings and prior observations.

claim: The results are compatible with the recently proposed 'ground state theory of cancer initiation'.
source: Furthermore, the results reported here are compatible with the recently proposed 'ground state theory of cancer initiation' (Jassim et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a statement about compatibility with a prior theory supported by citation.

claim: According to the ground state theory, a malignant transformation may occur in a cell harboring an oncogenic mutation upon a change of its functional state (its 'ground state').
source: According to that theory a malignant transformation may occur in a cell harboring an oncogenic mutation upon a change of its functional state (its 'ground state').
evidence: This is a description of a prior theory.

claim: The transient activation of a reprogramming factor (i.e. Ventx, Nanog, or Oct4) possibly synergizes with the oncogene to alter the epigenetic and functional state of the cell allowing its transformation into a tumorigenic cell.
source: Here, the transient activation of a reprogramming factor (i.e. Ventx, Nanog, or Oct4) possibly synergizes with the oncogene to alter the epigenetic and functional state of the cell allowing its transformation into a tumorigenic cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Stochastic and random tumor development over weeks following activation of kRasG12V in a whole tissue has been reported in brain, pancreas, and intestine.
source: This may also explain the apparent discrepancy between the present deterministic and rapid tumor development upon activation in a single cell of both kRasG12V and a reprogramming factor and the reports of stochastic and random tumor development over weeks following activation of kRasG12V in a whole tissue (brain [Ju et al., 2015], pancreas [Oh and Park, 2019], or intestine [Lu et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings supported by citations.

claim: In cases of whole tissue kRasG12V activation, transformed cells may have been triggered to undergo a malignant transformation by the stochastic activation of a reprogramming factor/Epi-Driver.
source: In the latter case, transformed cells may have been triggered to undergo a malignant transformation by the stochastic activation of a reprogramming factor/Epi-Driver, which is consistent with the recent finding that cancer initiation might occur by transient perturbations of epigenetic regulators (Parreno et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain prior findings, supported by citation.

claim: The progeny of the cell(s) of origin of cancer display a short-range dispersal within the tissue during the earliest phases of tumorigenesis and prior to the effective appearance of tumor mass.
source: Importantly, our observation that the progeny of the cell(s) of origin of cancer display a short-range dispersal within the tissue during the earliest phases of tumorigenesis and prior to the effective appearance of tumor mass corroborates a recent theoretical model predicting such an early dispersal during carcinogenesis to explain heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and tumor relapse (Waclaw et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an observation that corroborates a prior theoretical model, supported by citation.

claim: The optogenetic approach allows for the first experiments to predictably and noninvasively control the malignant transformation of a single cell in an unaltered microenvironment.
source: Being the first experiments to predictably and noninvasively control the malignant transformation of a single cell in an unaltered microenvironment, our approach opens a new vista on the study of 'the cell of origin of cancer' (Blanpain, 2013), an acknowledged enigma of cancer research.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty and significance of the approach.

claim: The optogenetic approach opens the way for a quantitative study of the initial stages of cancer at the single-cell level.
source: By allowing for specific and reproducible single-cell malignant transformation in vivo, our optogenetic approach opens the way for a quantitative study of the initial stages of cancer at the single-cell level (e.g. tracking and characterization), that will allow one to address many of these questions.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the approach.

claim: The Tg(actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP) transgenic line was generated by injecting the plasmid pT24-actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP with tol2 mRNA transposase.
source: The Tg(actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP) was generated by injecting the plasmid pT24-actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP, which contains the homologous cDNA sequence of KRASG12V from human, with tol2 mRNA transposase.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used to generate the transgenic line.

claim: Founder transgenic fish were identified by global expression of Eos.
source: Founder transgenic fish were identified by global expression of Eos.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used to identify transgenic fish.

claim: The Tg(ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP) line was previously described by Mosimann et al., 2011.
source: The Tg(ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP) was previously described (Mosimann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a citation to prior work describing the transgenic line.

claim: The double transgenic line was created by crossing Tg(actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP) and Tg(ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP).
source: The double transgenic line Tg(actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP; ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP) was created by crossing Tg(actin:loxP-EOS-stop-loxP-KRASG12V-T2A-H2B-mTFP) and Tg(ubi:Cre-ERT; myl7:EGFP).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used to create the double transgenic line.

claim: Founder double transgenic fish were selected by global expression of Eos and expression of EGFP in the developing heart.
source: Founder double transgenic fish were selected by global expression of Eos and expression of EGFP in the developing heart.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used to select double transgenic fish.

claim: To induce KRASG12V expression, 24 hpf embryos were incubated in 6 μM cCYC for 1 hr in the dark, rinsed in E3 medium followed by 5 min photoactivation with an ~365 nm UV lamp.
source: To induce kRASG12V expression, 24 hpf embryos were incubated in 6 μM cCYC for 1 hr (in the dark), rinsed in E3 medium followed by 5 min photoactivation with an ~365 nm UV lamp (measured intensity: 4 mW/cm2).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: Localized uncaging was performed by illumination for 7 min on a Nikon Ti microscope equipped with a light source peaking at 405 nm.
source: Localized uncaging was performed by illumination for 7 min on a Nikon Ti microscope equipped with a light source peaking at 405 nm, Figure 1.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol with reference to a figure.

claim: The size of the uncaging region was controlled by an iris that defines a circular illumination of diameter ~80 μm.
